        ### Question
        A 75-year-old woman, with menopause at 52 years of age, with no family or personal history of a fracture, diagnosed with temporal arteritis, who is going to start treatment with prednisone at high doses and with an expectation of treatment for at least one year. The delay of densitometry (DXA) in its center is 4-5 months. Preventive treatment of osteoporosis is proposed. Among the following, which is the most appropriate attitude ?:

        ### Options
        opa. Request DXA and wait for the result.
opb. Assess absolute risk of fracture using the FRAX questionnaire without BMD and treat only if it is high.
opc. Start treatment with bisphosphonates and vitamin D (800 IU / day).
opd. Administer calcium supplement (1g) and vitamin D (800 IU / day).
ope. Assess if you have osteopenia on the radiographs and treat if it is present.

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: "Temporal arteritis" -> "increased risk of osteoporosis due to chronic inflammation" -> "increased risk of fracture" -> "high-dose prednisone treatment" -> "further increases risk of osteoporosis and fracture" -> "need for preventive osteoporosis treatment" -> "delayed densitometry (DXA) by 4-5 months" -> "need for immediate preventive treatment" -> "start treatment without DXA" -> "appropriate attitude is to start treatment with bisphosphonates and vitamin D (800 IU/day)" -> 95%

(Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry)-DIAGNOSES->(Atherosclerosis)-ASSOCIATED_WITH->(Genes)-PART_OF->(Cartilage)-LOCATION_OF->(Prophylactic treatment)
